sources.text:
Gemspring Capital Management, the Westport, Connecticut-based middle-market private equity firm, has closed Gemspring Capital Fund IV at $3.5 billion. The firm said the fund was oversubscribed and reached its hard cap in less than three months, holding a single close for all institutional limited partner commitments.

The fund came in well above its $3 billion target, which was itself about 75% larger than the $1.7 billion Gemspring raised for Fund III, according to earlier fundraising reports. Founder and CEO Bret Wiener credited existing and new LPs, the team, and the firm’s track record of building businesses.

Consistent with prior vintages, Gemspring’s team made a substantial commitment of its own and is Fund IV’s largest single investor. The firm also runs Gemspring Growth Solutions, a non-control strategy that closed its second fund at $1.1 billion in 2025, and now has about $9 billion of capital under management. Sidley Austin served as legal counsel.

Gemspring targets companies with up to $2 billion in revenue across aerospace and defense, business services, consumer services, financial and insurance services, healthcare, industrials, software and tech-enabled services, offering both control buyouts and flexible capital solutions.

The speed of the raise stands out in a fundraising market where many managers are spending well over a year on the road. A single close at hard cap points to continued LP concentration in established middle-market managers with strong distributions and meaningful GP commitments, even as capital for newer and larger buyout franchises remains harder to secure.
